entries.subject: NASA Science Makemake overview
entries.finding: The display sphere uses the approximate 715 km radius from NASA Science, which also supplies the 22.5-hour rotation, 305-year orbital period and 45.8 AU average distance recorded as content.

entries.subject: Ortiz et al. (2012) projected occultation axes
entries.finding: The measured projected axes of 1,430 +/-9 and 1,502 +/-45 km are recorded as a size comparison but not used for the displayed body, because the README states the sky-plane measurements do not uniquely define a three-dimensional shape or spin pole.
entries.revisitWhen: A published three-dimensional shape or spin-pole solution for Makemake becomes available.

entries.subject: Shared neutral gray for the unresolved surface
entries.finding: The Shape lens is painted with the shared neutral gray (#808080 sRGB) generated through the raster route's neutral-shape science kind; the README calls it a display convention rather than a measured colour or albedo, with no nomenclature and an arbitrary map edge.

entries.subject: Pinned JPL elements at the shared epoch
entries.finding: Orbital placement uses the existing pinned JPL elements at the shared 2026-09-04 epoch, as recorded under known problems.

entries.subject: Display pole, meridian and rotational ephemeris
entries.finding: The display pole and meridian are explicitly arbitrary and the reported rotation period is content only, driving no invented ephemeris.
entries.revisitWhen: A measured spin pole or longitude system for Makemake is published.
